newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end lower, but helped by BoE auction.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end lower, but helped by BoE auction.

text.p: UK gilts ended 2/32 lower on Tuesday after dipping in line with falling European bond markets, but the losses were stemmed by the Bank of England's announcement that next week's 8.0 percent gilt auction will be a smaller-than-expected 2.0 billion sterling.
"Gilts have been quite resilient in the face of downward pressure in Europe," said a gilts salesman. "They were helped by the fact the auction will only be 2.0 billion stg."
The September gilt futures contract settled at 114-04, 2/32 off on the day, and in the middle of the day's range.
"Gilts succumbed to general weakness in European markets," said Tom Rayner, economist at Societe Generale. "The market is looking forward to more significant data on Wednesday and Friday."

The market faces a hectic Wednesday morning, with UK June unemployment and PSBR data and May average earnings, accompanied by the minutes of the first meeting of the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee.
The committee raised official interest rates by 1/4 point to 6.5 percent at that meeting and did the same again at the July meeting.
Markets will be interested to see if the minutes disclose any differences of opinion among committee members.
M4 broad money supply data due on Friday could also provide direction, analysts said.

The gilt spread to Bunds at 10 years narrowed to 159 basis points from 164 on Monday. September short sterling ended 0.01 basis points lower at 92.83, implying official interest rates at around 7.20 percent in the third quarter compared with the present 6.75 percent.
